entities.name: Reginald de Cobham, 1st Baron Cobham
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Reginald (Reynold) de Cobham, 1st Baron Cobham of Sterborough (c. 1295–1361), was an English knight, diplomat, and soldier of the early Hundred Years’ War. He played a pivotal role in the diplomatic efforts of King Edward III, forging alliances and managing truces with key European powers. Cobham’s service in the Hundred Years’ War also led to his appointment as a Knight of the Garter, an honor bestowed upon him by the monarch himself.

As a member of the powerful Cobham family, Reginald de Cobham inherited a significant amount of land and influence, which he leveraged to further his own interests and those of his lordship. His diplomatic efforts were instrumental in securing key victories for the English army, most notably the Battle of Crécy in 1346. The battle marked a significant turning point in the war, with the English emerging victorious and their influence on the continent increased.

Despite his significant contributions to the Hundred Years’ War, Reginald de Cobham’s legacy extends beyond the battlefield. His involvement in the establishment of the Order of the Garter, a prestigious chivalric order, further solidified his place in English history. The order, which was founded by King Edward III, remains one of the most revered and exclusive knighthoods in the world today.

In conclusion, Reginald de Cobham's life and legacy serve as a testament to the power of diplomacy and military prowess in shaping the course of history. His influence on the Hundred Years’ War and the establishment of the Order of the Garter continues to be felt to this day, making him one of the most fascinating figures of the medieval era.
